title: Understanding the Rear Drive Axle and Differential
introduction:
The differential takes rotation arriving from the driveshaft and sends drive toward both rear wheels while letting them turn at different speeds. A corner is like runners taking different lanes: the outside wheel has farther to travel, so matching wheel speeds would make a simple turn an argument with the pavement.

I follow the drive path first, then use the illustrations to locate the housing mounts, vent and pictured cooling equipment. This overview explains construction and component relationships. Bearing adjustment, sealing, removal and cooling-system service require their matching procedures and specifications. The cooling illustration identifies the pictured equipment without establishing which vehicle configurations have it.

edits.text: Start with the rear axle's construction, then follow how its components carry drive to the wheels.
How the Rear Axle Is Built
The rear axle assembly uses the following housing, gear, bearing and differential arrangements:
An integral-type housing with a hypoid gear arrangement: the drive pinion's center sits below the ring gear's centerline.
edits.why: The offset between those centerlines is the defining layout to picture when reading the term hypoid.

edits.text: A hypoid gear pair consisting of an 8.8-inch ring gear and an overhung drive pinion supported by 2 opposed tapered roller bearings.
edits.why: The bearings locate the input pinion as it meshes with the much larger ring gear.

edits.text: A drive pinion collapsible spacer on the differential pinion shaft maintains pinion bearing preload; the pinion nut adjusts that preload.
edits.why: Preload is the bearing arrangement's initial load. It is a bearing setup relationship, rather than simply a description of how tight a nut feels.

edits.text: A cast center section closed by a cast differential housing cover.
edits.why: The center section houses the gear assembly, while the cover closes the housing.

edits.text: Silicone rubber based sealant forms the gasket between the differential housing and its cover.
edits.why: The sealing layer is formed at the cover joint.

edits.text: A threaded differential pinion shaft lock bolt secures the differential pinion shaft to the differential case.
edits.why: This internal shaft supports the differential pinion gears described in the drive path below.

edits.text: The differential case sits in the rear axle housing between 2 opposing differential bearings, retained by 2 removable bearing caps.
edits.why: These bearings support the rotating differential case within the housing.

edits.text: Differential bearing shims sit between the bearing cups and rear axle housing. They adjust differential bearing preload and ring gear backlash.
edits.why: Backlash is clearance between mating gear teeth; preload is the initial bearing load. The shims affect these distinct setup relationships.

edits.text: Traction-Lok limited-slip axles are listed with 3.15, 3.31 and 3.55 ratios.
edits.why: Identify the differential design as well as its ratio, because the listed designs have overlapping ratio availability.

edits.text: Torsen limited-slip axles are listed with 3.55 and 3.73 ratios.
edits.why: The differential type matters when choosing the applicable service information.

edits.text: The driveshaft delivers rotational torque through the drive pinion flange. The flange turns the drive pinion, which drives the ring gear bolted to the differential case; the direction of rotation determines the vehicle's direction of travel. Inside the case, differential pinion gears ride on the pinion shaft and mesh with the side gears. The halfshafts are splined to those side gears and carry drive toward the wheels. This arrangement lets the halfshafts turn at different speeds when needed, such as while cornering.
edits.why: I trace the route from flange to pinion, ring gear, case, internal gears and halfshafts. That separates the input drive pinion from the smaller differential pinion gears working inside the case.

edits.text: The Torsen rear differential carrier is serviced only as a complete assembly.
edits.why: Keep this service boundary attached to the Torsen design when using the general construction description.

The central highlighted housing sits between the halfshafts. Use the key to distinguish the rear mounts and vibration dampers, if equipped, from the front mounts near the input flange. The vent tube runs from the housing toward the spring area at the right of the drawing.

In the underside view, locate the pump between the exhaust silencers, the cooler across the rear of the vehicle, and the lines connecting them to the differential. The sensor callout identifies the electrical sensing component beside the differential's fluid connections.
